Thisted is a Danish municipality evaluated for its clinical quality in treating atrial fibrillation, as detailed in the Annual Report from the Atrial Fibrillation Database in Denmark (Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark) [^src1]. The report, published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram, or RKKP), covers the period from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, and assesses treatment quality and safety across all 98 Danish municipalities to support local benchmarking and decentralized quality development [^src1][^src2]. 

In the context of the national healthcare system's quality monitoring, Thisted is specifically noted for its performance on Indicator 4b, which measures adherence to safety practices when using Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) medications [^src1]. Thisted achieved a compliance rate of 95.0% (862 out of 907 eligible cases) [^src1]. This performance allowed the municipality to exactly meet the national standard threshold of ≥95%, earning a "Yes" (Ja) designation for successfully fulfilling the indicator [^src1]. 

Additionally, the municipality's data is tracked for indicators related to the early initiation of anticoagulation treatment (Indicator 1) and the prevention of ischemic stroke via anticoagulation (Indicator 5) [^src2]. In these specific municipal breakdowns, Thisted recorded a 0.2% rate (with a confidence interval of 0.0–0.7%) for one of the tracked metrics, alongside 10 out of 1,273 cases (0.8%) for a related measurement [^src2].
